rubric_selfcheck.clear_priorities: Satisfied in PRIORITY, which defines the evaluation order (C1 -> C2 -> C3 -> C4 -> C5), the one-violation override rule, conflict resolution when user prompts clash with C1/C2 accounting facts, and the default "good" label.
rubric_selfcheck.links_to_training_examples: Satisfied in EXAMPLES and BOUNDARIES, citing 15 real 8-character training IDs (e.g., 04b71730, 0ae6aa45, 0eea79a6, 13120e9df, 1947acad, 1bedba83, 284db98e, c09ec6bd) with gold labels, figures, and C-numbers.
rubric_selfcheck.clear_boundaries: Satisfied in BOUNDARIES (B1–B3), which details ambiguous training regions (unstated MXN currency, all-time vs. bounded multi-month totals, and platform deep links) with contrasting training IDs and explicit decision rules.
rubric_selfcheck.consistency_with_implementation: Satisfied across base_prompt and topic_advice: the exact C1–C5 rules, priorities, boundary resolutions, and D1–D15 references form the working judge prompt directly.
